content.text:
The machine-wide mutex is the `BenchMutex` class in **`src/agentic_hil/bench.py`**.

Key details:

- **`BenchMutex`** (`src/agentic_hil/bench.py`) implements the machine-wide mutex. It stores its lock files under one agreed, per-machine location, `~/.agentic-hil/device-locks` (deliberately *not* under a per-configuration `state_root`, since two sessions with different `state_root` values may still be the same physical bench — see `tests/test_bench_mutex.py`).
- It exposes `acquire()`/`acquire_named()`/`release()`/`release_all()`, which take/release OS-level locks per physical resource name (e.g. `probe:<serial>`, `com:<device>`, `can:<adapter>:<channel>`, or `physical:<resource_id>`), taking a whole declared set in one sorted, all-or-nothing acquisition and unwinding on failure (`BenchMutex.acquire`/`acquire_named` in `bench.py`).
- Contention raises `DeviceBusyError`, naming the current holder rather than silently blocking; waiting only happens if explicitly requested via `wait_s`.
- Because it's an OS-level lock, a crashed process releases the device immediately (no stale-lock recovery needed).

This mutex is consumed via the higher-level `Device`/`DeviceSet` abstractions in **`src/agentic_hil/devices.py`** (`Device.acquire`, `DeviceSet.acquire`), which derive a `lock_key` from hardware identity (probe serial, resource_id, serial device path, etc.) so that two config entries pointing at the same physical unit collapse to a single lock. The `HardwareCoordinator` (referenced in `tests/test_devices.py`) and CLI commands like `bench_run_start`/`grant`/`revoke` (`src/agentic_hil/cli.py`) go through this same `BenchMutex` to enforce exclusivity across separate processes/terminals on the machine.

Documentation of this design is in `docs/safety-model.md` ("Exclusivity per physical device is machine-wide and held for the whole run, kept in one agreed place...").
